CURBSIDE RECYCLING EDUCATION
In 2018, the Phoenix Public Works Department (PWD) created a new program
to help tackle recycling contamination at the curb. Oops/Shine-on, as it was
coined, is the department’s program to get boots on the ground inspecting
the contents of its residents’ recycling containers across the City. The
program is currently maintained by one Solid Waste Supervisor, one Lead
Solid Waste Environmental Specialist and seven Solid Waste Environmental
Specialists.
The purpose of this program is to educate residents on proper recycling
methods, reduce contamination being placed in recycling containers, reduce
operational expenses at the City’s recycling facilities, increase the amount of
material diverted from the landfill and maximize the environmental benefits
of Phoenix’s recycling program. An average of 35,000 Phoenix residents are
educated through this program on an annual basis.

The purpose of this program is to educate residents on proper recycling
methods, reduce contamination being placed in recycling containers, reduce

CITY STAFF RESPONSIBILITES
Educate residents on how to recycle properly.
Conduct weekly recycling container inspections
within the specified routes/neighborhoods.
Enter all data into an application.
Provide follow-up to residents, when requested.

PROGRAM PROCESS
Four different routes are inspected over six consecutive weeks.
An average of 4,500 addresses are located within the four routes.
One of the following tags is attached to recycling containers every
week to help educate residents.
1 Shine-On (Green tag) is left when 0% contamination is
found in the recycle container.
Oops (Yellow tag) is left when 1 – 19% contamination is
2
found in the recycle container.
Residents should leave container at curb for collection.
Reject (Orange tag) is left when 20% or more
3
contamination is found in the recycle container.
A courtesy collection is provided only during week 1 of the process for any
container with 20% or more contamination. After week one, residents are required
to remove contamination and wait until the next week for collection.

IMPORTANT NOTICE:
If any address receives four reject tags within the six week inspection period, the recycle container(s) is removed from the
property and the customer will be prohibited from participating in the recycling program for one year.
